methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA signals intentional distribution of AI fluency through community-engaged education infrastructure, creating potential peer learning networks beyond the university campus that could spread deeper capability across the metro region.

signals.title: RC-RV partners with ed2go to launch innovative, on-demand workforce training programs - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: On-demand workforce training through ed2go platforms represents shallow, platform-mediated AI adoption in underserved regions—providing access but not necessarily building deep local capability or sustainable AI fluency networks.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: AI pressure on Richmond's young workforce indicates the metro hub is experiencing concentrated adoption pressure similar to NoVA, potentially widening the capability gap with rural regions unless training infrastructure distributes effectively.

signals.title: Amid AI, Quantum Tech, Chesterfield County, Va., Invests in Cyber - govtech.com
signals.signal_reading: Chesterfield County's investment in cybersecurity amid AI and quantum technology signals deepening technical capability in the Richmond metro area, reinforcing concentration of advanced digital infrastructure in established hubs rather than distributed development.

signals.title: Norfolk arrest in deadly shooting made quickly with help of technology, officials say - 13newsnow.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk police deploying AI-assisted technology for rapid criminal investigation represents shallow, vendor-delivered capability—functional adoption without building local AI development capacity or transferable technical expertise in the Hampton Roads workforce.
